report.answer_text: The central idea of Oliver Goldsmith’s *The Deserted Village* is that a society does not truly prosper when a few grow wealthy at the expense of ordinary people. Goldsmith contrasts Auburn’s once lively village life with its later emptiness, mourning the loss of a community whose residents were forced to leave when a wealthy landowner took control of the land. (poetryfoundation.org)
